welcome.title: Welcome to AI Assistant 👋
welcome.description: Quick 2-minute tour of the main features. You can skip with Esc, or replay this tour any time using the Help button in the top bar.

sidebar.title: Sidebar — your toolbox
sidebar.description: Each item in this column opens a different mode. Below it you also see your saved conversations and the "New Chat" button.

conversations.title: 💬 Conversations
conversations.description: Chat with any of 6 AI providers: OpenAI, Claude, Grok, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Kimi. Attach documents (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for analysis, and ask for SVG charts — they render inline in the response. All conversations are auto-saved and listed below.

verifier.title: ✓ Verify Response
verifier.description: Get an answer from one AI provider and have it fact-checked by a second one. Example: send a prompt to OpenAI, then have DeepSeek verify the response — useful for catching hallucinations or numeric mistakes.

compare.title: ⚖️ Compare Response
compare.description: Send the same prompt to two AI providers simultaneously and view their answers side-by-side. Great for picking the best wording, catching disagreements, or evaluating which model fits a task.

promptLibrary.title: 📚 Prompt Library
promptLibrary.description: Save your best or most-used prompts for reuse. Organize them in folders, then pick one from the library and it drops straight into the prompt input — ready to send or tweak.

skills.title: 🎯 Skills
skills.description: Skills teach the assistant tasks it can carry out — produce a document, convert a file, analyse a spreadsheet. Each is a folder of instructions and Python scripts that runs in your browser on your local folder. Ask, and the assistant picks the right one.

libraries.title: 📚 Libraries
libraries.description: Everything you reuse lives here: prompts, skills, agents, playbooks, code components and MCP servers. Click to open the list, pick a library and its content appears below.

workflows.title: 🔀 Workflows
workflows.description: Orchestrate agents, dispatchers, playbooks and code into multi-step workflows, test them step by step, and start them from a prompt, a schedule or an event. Then compile any workflow into standalone Python for LangGraph, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework or NVIDIA OO Agents.

fileStorage.title: 📁 File Storage
fileStorage.description: Browse the local folder dedicated to this app on your computer — the same folder where workflow outputs are written. Feed files back into conversations whenever you need them.

tools.title: Show / hide the sidebar
tools.description: Toggles the left sidebar we just walked through (Conversations, Verify, Compare, Prompt Library, Skills, Workflows, File Storage). Hide it to give the conversation more horizontal space; show it again whenever you need to switch tools.

help.title: Help — replay this tour
help.description: Click here any time to walk through this tour again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Manage your API keys, default model per provider, MCP servers, storage providers, and account preferences.

merge.title: Merge responses
merge.description: When checked, the conversation is preserved when you switch AI provider — useful for asking a different model to continue, refine, or critique the previous answer. When unchecked, switching providers clears the chat to start fresh.

viewFunctions.title: View Functions
viewFunctions.description: Opens a panel listing every tool/function the active AI provider can call right now — built-in tools (web search, code execution…) plus any MCP server tools you have connected.

viewContext.title: View Context
viewContext.description: Inspect exactly what is being sent to the AI: the system prompt, the message history (recent turns), and any attachments. Handy for debugging unexpected answers or checking how much context the model is seeing.

input.title: Prompt area
input.description: Type your message here. Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.

attach.title: Attach files 📎
attach.description: Click to attach files: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, plus text/markdown/CSV/JSON and images. You can also drag & drop files directly onto the conversation area — same result.

send.title: Send
send.description: Or click here to send your message. That's it — you're ready to go!

nooaSetup.title: NVIDIA OO Agents — one-time setup
nooaSetup.body: The Python runtime in {{folder}}/python does not include NOOA. To run NOOA workflows from SynergyAI, add it once: open a terminal in {{folder}}/python and run:
nooaSetup.note: Then select "Run" again in the canvas top menu. To run a NOOA workflow on another machine, Export it and follow the README.md in the zip.
nooaSetup.codeAct: NOOA agents answer by writing and executing Python code (CodeAct): run them in an environment you trust, ideally a container or VM.

runnerSetup.title: Python runtime not installed
runnerSetup.checked: What this check found in the folder
runnerSetup.body: Generated scripts run from the "python" folder inside {{folder}}, the folder you picked for SynergyAI. That folder needs a Python virtual environment once — a browser cannot create one. Open a terminal in {{folder}}/python and run:
runnerSetup.copyFailed: Could not copy the Python runner (main.py, requirements.txt) into {{folder}}/python: {{error}}. Check that SynergyAI still has access to that folder, then try again.
runnerSetup.regrant: Your browser needs your permission again to use the {{folder}} folder (browsers forget it after a restart). Click "Allow access to {{folder}}", then choose "Allow" in the browser prompt.
runnerSetup.pickFolder: SynergyAI has no local folder yet. Click "Choose folder", select your SynergyAI folder (usually Documents/synergyAI, or create it), then choose "Allow" in the browser prompt.
runnerSetup.unsupported: Compiled workflows run on your computer, which needs a browser that can use local folders. Open SynergyAI in Chrome, Edge or Brave and try again.
runnerSetup.ready: Close this and select "Generate" again in the canvas top menu.
runnerSetup.note: That builds one shared venv for the LangGraph, ADK and MAF runtimes (a NOOA package lists its own pip command at the top of its generated script). Then, from the same folder, start the runner with {{startCmd}} — not bare python3, or the scripts run without their packages. After it finishes, select "Generate" again in the canvas top menu.

swarmError.title: This workflow cannot run as a swarm
swarmError.neededText: one agent tagged Dispatcher, connected to two or more agents.
swarmError.note: In swarm mode the Dispatcher is not an agent — its prompt becomes the handoff guide every member carries.
swarmError.playbook: This workflow contains a Playbook node, which swarm mode does not support yet.
swarmError.outputs: There is more than one Output node. A swarm produces one answer.
swarmError.startNeedsTwo: Start is connected to fewer than two agents. A swarm is the agents drawn from Start, so connect at least two of them to it.
swarmError.dispatcherTag: An agent is tagged Dispatcher. In a swarm every member routes, so the tag has no meaning here — remove the Dispatcher tag and connect the agents to Start directly.
swarmError.neededFanout: two or more agents connected directly to Start. Each one can hand the conversation to the others.
swarmError.noteFanout: The prompt you type goes to whichever agent is holding the turn. The first prompt of a conversation goes to the first agent connected to Start.
swarmError.notOnStart: This agent is not connected to Start, so it is not in the swarm. Connect it to Start, or remove it.
swarmError.duplicateNames: Two agents share a name. A handoff names its target, so the swarm could not tell them apart — rename one.
swarmError.rewriteUnavailable: The swarm rules could not be loaded. Reload the page; if it persists, the editor's swarm-rewrite script is missing.
swarmError.rewriteFailed: The swarm rules could not read this canvas. The browser console has the details.
